newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds fall, hit by punt/sterling weakness.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds fall, hit by punt/sterling weakness.

text.p: Irish government bonds wilted in busy trade on Friday, undermined by worries about the Irish pound's weakness against sterling, dealers said.

"Strong defensive selling in Irish bonds has been a feature of the market since the UK rate cut and drop in sterling/Irish rate. Bond prices in the middle of the curve were heaviest hit with 50-60 basis points losses," one dealer said.
By 1537 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was 70p weaker at 105.60 to yield 6.24 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 60p at 106.75 to yield 6.90 percent.

"Everything depends on the currency market now. The Irish bond market virtually ignored the data in the U.S. because all trading was being influenced by the falling punt and possible inflationary pressures in Ireland," the dealer said.
Dealers said the market would be monitoring currency market developments next week, as well as data.
"We've got the CBI survey in the UK next week, and in the U.S. we also have third quarter non-farm payrolls and consumer credit figures," one said.
